rules.section_title: APB4 to TL-UL Bridge Design Specification
rules.quote: Every mandatory requirement has a stable REQ-- identifier and a verification method.
rules.statement: Every mandatory requirement has a stable REQ-- identifier and a verification method.

rules.section_title: APB4 to TL-UL Bridge Design Specification
rules.quote: Important limitation, read first: the bridge accepts only full-strobe writes (PSTRB = 4'b1111) and word-aligned addresses (PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00).
rules.statement: The bridge accepts only full-strobe writes (PSTRB = 4'b1111) and word-aligned addresses (PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00).

rules.section_title: APB4 to TL-UL Bridge Design Specification
rules.quote: A write with any other PSTRB value, and any access with a misaligned address, completes with PSLVERR = 1 and no TL-UL request is issued (DEC-001, REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002).
rules.condition: A write has a PSTRB value other than 4'b1111
rules.statement: A write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111 must complete with PSLVERR = 1.

rules.section_title: APB4 to TL-UL Bridge Design Specification
rules.quote: A write with any other PSTRB value, and any access with a misaligned address, completes with PSLVERR = 1 and no TL-UL request is issued (DEC-001, REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002).
rules.condition: An access has a misaligned address
rules.statement: Any access with a misaligned address must complete with PSLVERR = 1.

rules.section_title: APB4 to TL-UL Bridge Design Specification
rules.quote: A write with any other PSTRB value, and any access with a misaligned address, completes with PSLVERR = 1 and no TL-UL request is issued (DEC-001, REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002).
rules.condition: A write has PSTRB other than 4'b1111, or any access has a misaligned address
rules.statement: No TL-UL request is issued for a write with unsupported PSTRB or for a misaligned access.

rules.section_title: APB4 to TL-UL Bridge Design Specification
rules.quote: Software that needs byte or half-word writes must use a different bridge.
rules.condition: Software needs byte or half-word writes
rules.statement: Software needing byte or half-word writes must use a different bridge.

rules.quote: Each APB transfer becomes one TL-UL request, and the TL-UL response becomes the APB completion.
rules.statement: Each APB transfer must become exactly one TL-UL request, and the TL-UL response must become the APB completion.

rules.quote: The design goals are low latency and clean timing: the TL-UL request is launched from flip-flops in the first APB access cycle (see "early launch" in section 5.3), every output that changes toward either bus comes directly from a flip-flop, there is one clock domain, and the APB-facing logic and the TL-UL-facing logic are in separate modules. Feature ID: FEAT-003; Feature: Early launch of the TL-UL request from flip-flops; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-001, REQ-PERF-001
rules.statement: The TL-UL request must be launched from flip-flops in the first APB access cycle (early launch).

rules.quote: The design goals are low latency and clean timing: the TL-UL request is launched from flip-flops in the first APB access cycle (see "early launch" in section 5.3), every output that changes toward either bus comes directly from a flip-flop, there is one clock domain, and the APB-facing logic and the TL-UL-facing logic are in separate modules.
rules.statement: Every output that changes toward either bus must come directly from a flip-flop.

rules.quote: Excluded: partial writes (any PSTRB other than 4'b1111); byte or half-word accesses; TL-UL bursts and multiple outstanding requests; the TL-UL-to-APB direction; TL-UL bus integrity generation or checking; a response timeout (the SoC watchdog handles a device that never responds, DEC-003); address decoding or protection; clock-domain crossing; software-visible registers.
rules.statement: The bridge does not support partial writes (PSTRB other than 4'b1111), byte or half-word accesses, TL-UL bursts, or multiple outstanding requests.

rules.quote: Feature ID: FEAT-001; Feature: APB4 full-strobe write to TL-UL PutFullData; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-002
rules.statement: An APB4 full-strobe write must be converted to a TL-UL PutFullData request.

rules.quote: Feature ID: FEAT-002; Feature: APB4 read to TL-UL Get; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-003
rules.statement: An APB4 read must be converted to a TL-UL Get request.

rules.quote: Feature ID: FEAT-004; Feature: Local error response for unsupported strobe or misaligned address; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002
rules.statement: The bridge must give a local error response for an unsupported strobe or misaligned address.

rules.quote: Feature ID: FEAT-005; Feature: TL-UL response checking and error mapping; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-ERR-003 to REQ-ERR-005
rules.statement: The bridge must check the TL-UL response and map errors to PSLVERR.

rules.quote: Feature ID: FEAT-006; Feature: Back-to-back APB transfers with PSEL held high; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-008, REQ-PERF-004
rules.statement: The bridge must support back-to-back APB transfers with PSEL held high.

rules.quote: Ref ID: REF-003; Document and revision: VLSIT RTL Design Rules v2, VLSIT_RTL_Design_Rule.md; Applicable clauses: All applicable rules; Authority / notes: Mandatory RTL coding, hierarchy, reset, CDC and naming baseline
rules.statement: The RTL design must follow the VLSIT RTL Design Rules v2 (REF-003) as the mandatory coding, hierarchy, reset, CDC and naming baseline.

rules.quote: This specification defines the IP contract and shall stay consistent with REF-001, REF-002 and REF-003.
rules.statement: This specification must stay consistent with REF-001, REF-002 and REF-003.

rules.quote: REF-003 is the mandatory RTL coding baseline.
rules.statement: REF-003 is the mandatory RTL coding baseline and the RTL must comply with it.

rules.quote: Standard: AMBA APB; Revision / profile: APB4 (REF-001 Issue D; PPROT, PSTRB, PSLVERR; no PWAKEUP, no user or parity signals); Role implemented: Completer (subordinate); Options: Wait states through PREADY; Deviations: PPROT is accepted and ignored (DEC-007). PSTRB other than 4'b1111 on a write is rejected with PSLVERR (DEC-001). Misaligned PADDR is rejected with PSLVERR (REF-001 chapter 2 leaves it UNPREDICTABLE)
rules.condition: A write transfer with PSTRB other than 4'b1111
rules.statement: The bridge must reject a write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111 by responding with PSLVERR.

rules.quote: Standard: AMBA APB; Revision / profile: APB4 (REF-001 Issue D; PPROT, PSTRB, PSLVERR; no PWAKEUP, no user or parity signals); Role implemented: Completer (subordinate); Options: Wait states through PREADY; Deviations: PPROT is accepted and ignored (DEC-007). PSTRB other than 4'b1111 on a write is rejected with PSLVERR (DEC-001). Misaligned PADDR is rejected with PSLVERR (REF-001 chapter 2 leaves it UNPREDICTABLE)
rules.statement: The bridge must reject a transfer with misaligned PADDR by responding with PSLVERR.

rules.quote: Standard: AMBA APB; Revision / profile: APB4 (REF-001 Issue D; PPROT, PSTRB, PSLVERR; no PWAKEUP, no user or parity signals); Role implemented: Completer (subordinate); Options: Wait states through PREADY; Deviations: PPROT is accepted and ignored (DEC-007). PSTRB other than 4'b1111 on a write is rejected with PSLVERR (DEC-001). Misaligned PADDR is rejected with PSLVERR (REF-001 chapter 2 leaves it UNPREDICTABLE)
rules.statement: PPROT must be accepted and ignored; it must not affect bridge behavior.

rules.quote: Standard: TileLink Uncached Lightweight (OpenTitan profile); Revision / profile: REF-002, 32-bit data, a_size = 2 only, no bursts; Role implemented: Host (manager); Options: a_user driven to zero, no integrity (DEC-004); Deviations: d_param, d_size, d_sink and d_user are present as ports but unused (DEC-006)
rules.statement: The TL-UL host side must use a_size = 2 only, with 32-bit data and no bursts.

rules.quote: Standard: TileLink Uncached Lightweight (OpenTitan profile); Revision / profile: REF-002, 32-bit data, a_size = 2 only, no bursts; Role implemented: Host (manager); Options: a_user driven to zero, no integrity (DEC-004); Deviations: d_param, d_size, d_sink and d_user are present as ports but unused (DEC-006)
rules.statement: a_user must be driven to zero, with no integrity.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the APB side is idle and i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 (Setup phase), the bridge shall capture the request at the rising edge that ends that cycle and, when the request is legal, shall present it on the TL-UL channel A from flip-flops in the next cycle (the first Access cycle).; Source: REF-001 4.1, Appendix A; DEC-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-006; assertion SVA-008
rules.condition: APB side idle, i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 (Setup phase)
rules.statement: The bridge shall capture the request at the rising edge ending the Setup cycle.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the APB side is idle and i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 (Setup phase), the bridge shall capture the request at the rising edge that ends that cycle and, when the request is legal, shall present it on the TL-UL channel A from flip-flops in the next cycle (the first Access cycle).; Source: REF-001 4.1, Appendix A; DEC-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-006; assertion SVA-008
rules.statement: The bridge shall present the request on TL-UL channel A from flip-flops in the next cycle (first Access cycle).

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall convert an APB write with PSTRB = 4'b1111 and PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00 into one TL-UL PutFullData (a_opcode = 3'b000) with a_size = 2, a_mask = 4'b1111, a_address = PADDR and a_data = PWDATA.; Source: REF-002 usage of opcode, size and mask; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002; assertion SVA-004
rules.condition: APB write with PSTRB = 4'b1111 and PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00
rules.statement: The bridge shall convert it into one PutFullData (a_opcode = 3'b000) with a_size = 2, a_mask = 4'b1111, a_address = PADDR and a_data = PWDATA.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall convert an APB read with PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00 into one TL-UL Get (a_opcode = 3'b100) with a_size = 2, a_mask = 4'b1111 and a_address = PADDR. PSTRB is ignored on reads.; Source: REF-002; REF-001 3.2; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-006; assertion SVA-004
rules.statement: The bridge shall convert it into one TL-UL Get (a_opcode = 3'b100) with a_size = 2, a_mask = 4'b1111 and a_address = PADDR.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall convert an APB read with PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00 into one TL-UL Get (a_opcode = 3'b100) with a_size = 2, a_mask = 4'b1111 and a_address = PADDR. PSTRB is ignored on reads.; Source: REF-002; REF-001 3.2; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-006; assertion SVA-004
rules.statement: PSTRB shall be ignored on reads.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall have at most one TL-UL request outstanding and shall start no new request before the APB completion of the previous transfer.; Source: DEC-002; REF-005 pendingReqPerSrc; Applies to: All; Verification method: Assertion SVA-003; simulation TEST-013
rules.statement: The bridge shall have at most one TL-UL request outstanding.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall have at most one TL-UL request outstanding and shall start no new request before the APB completion of the previous transfer.; Source: DEC-002; REF-005 pendingReqPerSrc; Applies to: All; Verification method: Assertion SVA-003; simulation TEST-013
rules.statement: The bridge shall start no new TL-UL request before the APB completion of the previous transfer.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall keep o_tlul_a_valid high and channel A stable from the cycle after capture until i_tlul_a_ready is sampled high.; Source: REF-002 timing diagrams; REF-005; Applies to: All; Verification method: Assertion SVA-002; simulation TEST-009
rules.condition: From the cycle after capture until i_tlul_a_ready is sampled high
rules.statement: The bridge shall keep o_tlul_a_valid high and channel A stable.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall return the TL-UL d_data on o_apb_prdata for a read that completes without error and shall drive o_apb_prdata to 0 for a write completion and for every error completion.; Source: REF-001 3.3, 3.4; DEC-009; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-006, TEST-007
rules.statement: The bridge shall return the TL-UL d_data on o_apb_prdata.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall return the TL-UL d_data on o_apb_prdata for a read that completes without error and shall drive o_apb_prdata to 0 for a write completion and for every error completion.; Source: REF-001 3.3, 3.4; DEC-009; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-006, TEST-007
rules.condition: Write completion or any error completion
rules.statement: The bridge shall drive o_apb_prdata to 0.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-007; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall discard a TL-UL response that arrives when no request has been accepted (orphan response) without any effect on the APB side.; Source: REF-002 explicit error cases (orphaned responses discarded on the host side); Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-010; assertion SVA-009
rules.condition: TL-UL response arrives when no request has been accepted (orphan)
rules.statement: The bridge shall discard the response without any effect on the APB side.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-008; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall detect the Setup phase of a transfer from the levels i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 (not from an edge of i_apb_psel), and shall accept a new transfer whose Setup phase is in the cycle immediately after the PREADY cycle of the previous transfer, both when i_apb_psel stays 1 and only i_apb_penable changes level, and when i_apb_psel returns to 0 for one or more cycles in between. Every combination of read, write and error transfers shall be supported back to back.; Source: REF-001 3.1, 4.1 and Figure 4-1 (the bus moves directly from ACCESS to SETUP when another transfer follows); Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-019; assertion SVA-010
rules.statement: The bridge shall detect the Setup phase from levels i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0, not from an edge of i_apb_psel.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-008; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall detect the Setup phase of a transfer from the levels i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 (not from an edge of i_apb_psel), and shall accept a new transfer whose Setup phase is in the cycle immediately after the PREADY cycle of the previous transfer, both when i_apb_psel stays 1 and only i_apb_penable changes level, and when i_apb_psel returns to 0 for one or more cycles in between. Every combination of read, write and error transfers shall be supported back to back.; Source: REF-001 3.1, 4.1 and Figure 4-1 (the bus moves directly from ACCESS to SETUP when another transfer follows); Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-019; assertion SVA-010
rules.condition: New Setup phase in the cycle immediately after the PREADY cycle, whether psel stays 1 or returns to 0 for one or more cycles
rules.statement: The bridge shall accept the new transfer.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-FUNC-008; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall detect the Setup phase of a transfer from the levels i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 (not from an edge of i_apb_psel), and shall accept a new transfer whose Setup phase is in the cycle immediately after the PREADY cycle of the previous transfer, both when i_apb_psel stays 1 and only i_apb_penable changes level, and when i_apb_psel returns to 0 for one or more cycles in between. Every combination of read, write and error transfers shall be supported back to back.; Source: REF-001 3.1, 4.1 and Figure 4-1 (the bus moves directly from ACCESS to SETUP when another transfer follows); Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-019; assertion SVA-010
rules.statement: Every combination of read, write and error transfers shall be supported back to back.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-IF-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall expose exactly the APB4 Completer signals listed in section 6.2 and no other APB signal.; Source: REF-001 chapter 2; REF-003 PRT-01, PRT-03; Applies to: All; Verification method: Lint and port-list review: TEST-016
rules.statement: The bridge shall expose exactly the APB4 Completer signals listed in section 6.2 and no other APB signal.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-IF-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall expose exactly the TL-UL host signals listed in section 6.2 (the full OpenTitan signal set; d_param, d_size, d_sink and d_user are unused, DEC-006) and no other.; Source: REF-002 signals; DEC-006; Applies to: All; Verification method: Lint and port-list review: TEST-016
rules.statement: The bridge shall expose exactly the TL-UL host signals listed in section 6.2 and no others.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-IF-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: Every output port that changes value during operation shall be driven directly by the Q pin of a flip-flop, with no combinational logic between the flip-flop and the port. Outputs that never change after reset are constant tie-offs (DEC-005).; Source: Product requirement; DEC-005; Applies to: All; Verification method: Structural check of the RTL and the synthesized netlist: TEST-017
rules.condition: Output port changes value during operation
rules.statement: Such output ports shall be driven directly by a flip-flop Q pin with no combinational logic; never-changing outputs are constant tie-offs.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-IF-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall assert o_apb_pready for exactly one cycle per transfer, and only in an Access cycle (i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 1). o_apb_pslverr shall be 1 only while o_apb_pready is 1.; Source: REF-001 3.1, 3.4; Applies to: All; Verification method: Assertion SVA-001; APB protocol checker
rules.statement: The bridge shall assert o_apb_pready for exactly one cycle per transfer, and only in an Access cycle (psel = 1, penable = 1).

rules.quote: ID: REQ-IF-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall assert o_apb_pready for exactly one cycle per transfer, and only in an Access cycle (i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 1). o_apb_pslverr shall be 1 only while o_apb_pready is 1.; Source: REF-001 3.1, 3.4; Applies to: All; Verification method: Assertion SVA-001; APB protocol checker
rules.statement: o_apb_pslverr shall be 1 only while o_apb_pready is 1.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-IF-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall drive o_tlul_a_param = 3'b000, o_tlul_a_size = 2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask = 4'b1111, o_tlul_a_source = PARA_SRC_ID and o_tlul_a_user = '0 (all bits zero) on every request.; Source: REF-002; DEC-004; Applies to: All; Verification method: Assertion SVA-005
rules.statement: The bridge shall drive a_param = 3'b000, a_size = 2'b10, a_mask = 4'b1111, a_source = PARA_SRC_ID and a_user = '0.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-IF-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall drive o_tlul_d_ready low in reset and high from the first clock edge after reset release, and shall keep it high.; Source: DEC-010; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-001; assertion SVA-006
rules.statement: The bridge shall drive o_tlul_d_ready low.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-IF-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall drive o_tlul_d_ready low in reset and high from the first clock edge after reset release, and shall keep it high.; Source: DEC-010; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-001; assertion SVA-006
rules.condition: From first clock edge after reset release
rules.statement: The bridge shall drive o_tlul_d_ready high and keep it high.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-IF-007; Requirement using shall/should/may: The APB-facing logic and the TL-UL-facing logic shall be in two separate modules that are connected only through the internal interface of section 5.1.; Source: Product requirement; Applies to: All; Verification method: Design review and hierarchy check: TEST-017
rules.statement: APB-facing and TL-UL-facing logic shall be in two separate modules connected only through the internal interface of section 5.1.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-ERR-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: When a write has PSTRB other than 4'b1111, the bridge shall issue no TL-UL request and shall complete the transfer with PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle.; Source: DEC-001; REF-001 3.4; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-004
rules.statement: The bridge shall issue no TL-UL request and complete with PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-ERR-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: When PADDR[1:0] is not 2'b00 (read or write), the bridge shall issue no TL-UL request and shall complete the transfer with PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle.; Source: REF-001 chapter 2 (unaligned address UNPREDICTABLE); DEC-001; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-005
rules.statement: The bridge shall issue no TL-UL request and complete with PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-ERR-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the TL-UL response has d_error = 1, the bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.; Source: REF-002 explicit error cases; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-007
rules.statement: The bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-ERR-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the TL-UL response has a d_opcode other than AccessAckData (3'b001) for a read, or other than AccessAck (3'b000) for a write, the bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.; Source: REF-005 respOpcode; DEC-008; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-008
rules.condition: Response d_opcode is not AccessAckData (3'b001) for a read or not AccessAck (3'b000) for a write
rules.statement: The bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-ERR-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the TL-UL response has d_source different from PARA_SRC_ID, the bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.; Source: REF-005 respMustHaveReq; DEC-008; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-008
rules.statement: The bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-CLK-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall operate in one clock domain, i_clk_core, for both interfaces and shall contain no clock-domain crossing.; Source: Section 7; Applies to: All; Verification method: CDC analysis: TEST-016
rules.statement: The bridge shall operate in one clock domain, i_clk_core, for both interfaces with no clock-domain crossing.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-RESET-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall use the active-low reset i_rst_n_core with asynchronous assertion and shall drive o_tlul_a_valid, o_tlul_d_ready, o_apb_pready, o_apb_prdata, o_apb_pslverr, o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address and o_tlul_a_data to 0 while the reset is asserted.; Source: REF-003 RST-01; DEC-010, DEC-013; Applies to: All; Verification method: Reset test: TEST-001
rules.statement: The bridge shall use active-low reset i_rst_n_core with asynchronous assertion.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-RESET-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall use the active-low reset i_rst_n_core with asynchronous assertion and shall drive o_tlul_a_valid, o_tlul_d_ready, o_apb_pready, o_apb_prdata, o_apb_pslverr, o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address and o_tlul_a_data to 0 while the reset is asserted.; Source: REF-003 RST-01; DEC-010, DEC-013; Applies to: All; Verification method: Reset test: TEST-001
rules.statement: The bridge shall drive the listed outputs to 0 while reset is asserted.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-RESET-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall abandon any transfer in progress when the reset is asserted and shall send no APB completion for it after reset release.; Source: Section 7.3; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-012
rules.statement: The bridge shall abandon the transfer and send no APB completion for it after reset release.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PARAM-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall accept only the parameter values listed in section 8; an illegal value shall be reported at elaboration of the verification source set.; Source: Section 8; Applies to: All; Verification method: Elaboration check: TEST-014
rules.statement: The bridge shall accept only parameter values listed in section 8; an illegal value shall be reported at elaboration.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PERF-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the TL-UL device accepts the request in the first cycle and returns the response in the following cycle, the APB Access phase shall last 3 cycles (2 wait states).; Source: Section 10.3; DEC-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-006
rules.condition: Device accepts request in first cycle and returns response in the following cycle
rules.statement: The APB Access phase shall last 3 cycles (2 wait states).

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PERF-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the device returns the response in the cycle in which it accepts the request, the APB Access phase shall last 2 cycles (1 wait state).; Source: Section 10.3; REF-005 (response in the acceptance cycle allowed); Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-011
rules.condition: Device returns response in the cycle it accepts the request
rules.statement: The APB Access phase shall last 2 cycles (1 wait state).

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PERF-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: A local error completion (REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002) shall last 1 Access cycle (no wait state), and a new Setup phase shall be accepted in the cycle after PREADY.; Source: Section 10.3, 10.4; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-004, TEST-005, TEST-013
rules.statement: The completion shall last 1 Access cycle with no wait state.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PERF-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: A local error completion (REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002) shall last 1 Access cycle (no wait state), and a new Setup phase shall be accepted in the cycle after PREADY.; Source: Section 10.3, 10.4; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-004, TEST-005, TEST-013
rules.statement: A new Setup phase shall be accepted in the cycle after PREADY.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PERF-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: With i_apb_psel held high, back-to-back transfers shall run at the same minimum Setup-to-Setup interval as with a gap: 4 cycles with a prompt device, 3 cycles with a same-cycle response and 2 cycles after a local error, with no idle cycle added by the bridge.; Source: Section 10.4; REQ-FUNC-008; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-019
rules.statement: Setup-to-Setup interval shall be the minimum: 4 cycles with prompt device, 3 with same-cycle response, 2 after local error, with no idle cycle added.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-RTL-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and shall use the hierarchy of section 14.2.; Source: REF-003; Applies to: All; Verification method: Lint and review: TEST-016
rules.statement: The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and use the hierarchy of section 14.2.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-VER-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: An APB protocol checker and the TL-UL protocol checker of REF-005 shall be bound to the ports in every simulation.; Source: REF-001, REF-005; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation log review: TEST-015
rules.statement: An APB protocol checker and the REF-005 TL-UL protocol checker shall be bound to the ports.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-DFT-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The RTL shall be scan-insertable: no latch, no combinational loop, no internal tri-state, no clock gating and no gated or derived clock.; Source: REF-003 section 11; Applies to: All; Verification method: Lint and scan rule check: TEST-018
rules.statement: The RTL shall be scan-insertable: no latch, combinational loop, internal tri-state, clock gating, or gated/derived clock.

rules.quote: The data width is fixed at 32 bits; there is no data-width parameter (DEC-011).
rules.statement: The data width shall be fixed at 32 bits, with no data-width parameter.

rules.quote: Values of PARA_ADDR_W outside 16 to 32 are illegal (section 8).
rules.statement: PARA_ADDR_W must not be configured with a value outside the range 16 to 32.

rules.quote: They exchange one request bundle and one response bundle through internal wires, so neither module reads a port of the other bus.
rules.statement: m_apb_if and m_tlul_if exchange one request bundle and one response bundle through internal wires, and neither module reads a port of the other bus.

rules.quote: Wire: w_req_launch; Direction: m_apb_if to m_tlul_if; Width: 1; Meaning: Setup phase of a legal request: load channel A at the coming edge
rules.condition: Setup phase of a legal request
rules.statement: m_apb_if must assert w_req_launch to m_tlul_if during the Setup phase of a legal request so channel A is loaded at the coming edge.

rules.quote: Wire: w_resp_rdata; Direction: m_tlul_if to m_apb_if; Width: 32; Meaning: Read data, already forced to 0 for writes and for errors
rules.statement: w_resp_rdata must be forced to 0 for writes and for errors.

rules.quote: The bridge therefore captures the request at the end of the Setup cycle straight into the TL-UL channel A flip-flops. Channel A is valid in the first Access cycle, so the request reaches the TL-UL device one cycle after the Setup cycle, with no intermediate buffer stage.
rules.statement: The request is captured at the end of Setup straight into channel A flops, and channel A is valid in the first Access cycle, one cycle after Setup, with no buffer stage.

rules.quote: At the end of S, a legal request is loaded into the A-channel flops and reg_a_valid is set; an illegal request instead loads the response flops with PSLVERR = 1 and PREADY = 1.
rules.condition: End of Setup cycle with a legal request
rules.statement: At the end of the Setup phase a legal request must be loaded into the A-channel flops and reg_a_valid set.

rules.quote: At the end of S, a legal request is loaded into the A-channel flops and reg_a_valid is set; an illegal request instead loads the response flops with PSLVERR = 1 and PREADY = 1.
rules.condition: End of Setup cycle with an illegal request
rules.statement: At the end of the Setup phase an illegal request must load the response flops with PSLVERR = 1 and PREADY = 1.

rules.quote: Access 1 (A1): o_tlul_a_valid = 1 with the converted request, o_tlul_d_ready = 1.
rules.statement: In A1, o_tlul_a_valid must be 1 with the converted request and o_tlul_d_ready must be 1.

rules.quote: When i_tlul_a_ready = 1 the request is accepted at the end of A1.
rules.statement: When i_tlul_a_ready is 1 the request is accepted at the end of A1.

rules.quote: At the end of A2 the response is checked and loaded into reg_prdata, reg_pslverr and reg_pready.
rules.condition: End of A2 when response is returned
rules.statement: At the end of A2 the response is checked and loaded into reg_prdata, reg_pslverr and reg_pready.

rules.quote: Access 3 (A3): o_apb_pready = 1 with o_apb_prdata and o_apb_pslverr, all from flops. The transfer ends at the end of A3.
rules.statement: In A3, o_apb_pready must be 1 with o_apb_prdata and o_apb_pslverr driven directly from flops, and the transfer ends at the end of A3.

rules.quote: If the device answers in the cycle in which it accepts the request (A1), the response is loaded at the end of A1 and PREADY is 1 in A2.
rules.condition: Device answers in the cycle it accepts the request (A1)
rules.statement: If the device responds in A1, the response must be loaded at the end of A1 and PREADY must be 1 in A2.

rules.quote: If the device holds a_ready low, o_tlul_a_valid and channel A stay unchanged and the Access phase is extended; the same happens when the response is late.
rules.statement: If a_ready is low, o_tlul_a_valid and channel A must stay unchanged and the Access phase is extended; likewise for a late response.

rules.quote: An APB Requester that has another transfer for the same Completer keeps i_apb_psel at 1 after the last Access cycle and only drives i_apb_penable back to 0; the bus then moves directly from ACCESS to SETUP (REF-001 3.1, 4.1). The bridge supports this without any idle cycle. The reason is that the Setup phase is recognized by the levels i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 while the APB FSM is idle, not by a rising edge of i_apb_psel.
rules.condition: Back-to-back transfers with i_apb_psel held at 1
rules.statement: The bridge must support back-to-back transfers without an idle cycle, recognizing Setup by levels i_apb_psel=1 and i_apb_penable=0 while the APB FSM is idle, not by a psel rising edge.

rules.quote: The PREADY cycle of a transfer is also the cycle in which the APB FSM is in ENUM_ST_DONE, and the APB FSM is in ENUM_ST_IDLE again in the next cycle, which is the Setup cycle of the next transfer. The A-channel flops, the response flops and both FSMs are therefore free in time for the next capture, and the next transfer starts exactly like the first one.
rules.condition: After the PREADY cycle of a transfer
rules.statement: The APB FSM is in ENUM_ST_DONE in the PREADY cycle and in ENUM_ST_IDLE in the next cycle, so flops and FSMs are free for the next capture.

rules.quote: The same holds when the Requester releases i_apb_psel for one or more cycles in between.
rules.condition: Requester releases i_apb_psel for one or more cycles between transfers
rules.statement: Next transfers must start exactly like the first one when i_apb_psel is released for one or more cycles in between.

rules.quote: Figure 6-4 shows a write, a read and an illegal write one after the other with i_apb_psel held high.
rules.condition: Write, read and illegal write back to back with i_apb_psel held high
rules.statement: A write, a read and an illegal write must complete one after the other with i_apb_psel held high.

rules.quote: At most one TL-UL request is outstanding, and its a_source is PARA_SRC_ID.
rules.statement: At most one TL-UL request is outstanding, and its a_source is PARA_SRC_ID.

rules.quote: o_tlul_a_valid is high only in the TL-UL FSM state ENUM_ST_REQ, and channel A does not change while o_tlul_a_valid is high and i_tlul_a_ready is low.
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_valid must be high only in TL-UL FSM state ENUM_ST_REQ.

rules.quote: o_tlul_a_valid is high only in the TL-UL FSM state ENUM_ST_REQ, and channel A does not change while o_tlul_a_valid is high and i_tlul_a_ready is low.
rules.statement: Channel A must not change while o_tlul_a_valid is high and i_tlul_a_ready is low.

rules.quote: o_apb_pready is high only in the APB FSM state ENUM_ST_DONE, for one cycle.
rules.statement: o_apb_pready must be high only in APB FSM state ENUM_ST_DONE, for one cycle.

rules.quote: No TL-UL request is issued for an illegal APB request.
rules.statement: No TL-UL request may be issued for an illegal APB request.

rules.quote: The TL-UL FSM is idle whenever the APB FSM is idle.
rules.statement: The TL-UL FSM is idle whenever the APB FSM is idle.

rules.quote: Interface ID: IF-001; Type and revision: AMBA APB4 (REF-001 Issue D, APB4 subset); Role: Completer (subordinate); Direction at IP boundary: Requests in, completion out; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Required / optional: Required; Configurations: All
rules.statement: The bridge must provide the APB4 completer interface IF-001 (REF-001 Issue D APB4 subset) in CLK-CORE, required in all configurations.

rules.quote: Interface ID: IF-002; Type and revision: TL-UL, OpenTitan profile (REF-002); Role: Host (manager); Direction at IP boundary: Requests out, responses in; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Required / optional: Required; Configurations: All
rules.statement: The bridge must provide the TL-UL host interface IF-002 (OpenTitan profile, REF-002) in CLK-CORE, required in all configurations.

rules.quote: Interface ID: IF-003; Type and revision: Clock and reset; Role: Receiver; Direction at IP boundary: Inputs; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Required / optional: Required; Configurations: All
rules.statement: The bridge must provide the clock and reset input interface IF-003 in CLK-CORE, required in all configurations.

rules.quote: Port: i_apb_paddr; Direction: Input; Width: PARA_ADDR_W; Meaning (function): Byte address; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Data (valid with i_apb_psel); Reset / idle value: Not used in reset; Timing / sampling: Captured at the Setup edge; bits [1:0] must be 0; Configurations: All
rules.statement: i_apb_paddr bits [1:0] must be 0.

rules.quote: Port: i_apb_pstrb; Direction: Input; Width: 4; Meaning (function): Write strobes; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Data (valid with i_apb_psel); Reset / idle value: Not used in reset; Timing / sampling: Checked at the Setup edge; must be 4'b1111 for a write; Configurations: All
rules.condition: For an APB write at the Setup edge
rules.statement: i_apb_pstrb must be 4'b1111 for a write.

rules.quote: Port: o_apb_pready; Direction: Output (flop); Width: 1; Meaning (function): Transfer ready; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Pulse (1 cycle per transfer); Reset / idle value: 0; Timing / sampling: High for one cycle per transfer; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_apb_pready must be high for exactly one cycle per transfer and 0 in reset.

rules.quote: Port: o_apb_prdata; Direction: Output (flop); Width: 32; Meaning (function): Read data; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Data (valid with o_apb_pready); Reset / idle value: 0; Timing / sampling: Valid with o_apb_pready; holds its last value otherwise (DEC-009); Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_apb_prdata is valid with o_apb_pready and holds its last value otherwise; reset value is 0.

rules.quote: Port: o_apb_pslverr; Direction: Output (flop); Width: 1; Meaning (function): Transfer error; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Level (high only with o_apb_pready); Reset / idle value: 0; Timing / sampling: High only with o_apb_pready; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_apb_pslverr must not be high unless o_apb_pready is high.

rules.quote: Port: o_tlul_a_valid; Direction: Output (flop); Width: 1; Meaning (function): Request valid; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Level (set at the Setup edge, held until i_tlul_a_ready); Reset / idle value: 0; Timing / sampling: Set at the Setup edge, held until i_tlul_a_ready; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_valid is set at the Setup edge and held until i_tlul_a_ready; it is 0 in reset.

rules.quote: Port: o_tlul_a_opcode; Direction: Output; Width: 3; Meaning (function): Request opcode: bit 2 from a flop (1 = Get); bits [1:0] constant 0 (PutFullData 3'b000, Get 3'b100); Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Data (valid with o_tlul_a_valid); Reset / idle value: 0; Timing / sampling: Stable while valid; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_opcode bit 2 is 1 for Get and bits [1:0] are constant 0; it must be stable while o_tlul_a_valid is high.

rules.quote: Port: o_tlul_a_param; Direction: Output (constant); Width: 3; Meaning (function): Reserved, always 3'b000; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Static (constant 3'b000); Reset / idle value: 3'b000; Timing / sampling: Constant; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_param must always be 3'b000.

rules.quote: Port: o_tlul_a_size; Direction: Output (constant); Width: 2; Meaning (function): Request size, always 2'b10 (4 bytes); Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Static (constant 2'b10); Reset / idle value: 2'b10; Timing / sampling: Constant; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_size must always be 2'b10.

rules.quote: Port: o_tlul_a_source; Direction: Output (constant); Width: PARA_SRC_W; Meaning (function): Request identifier, always PARA_SRC_ID; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Static (constant PARA_SRC_ID); Reset / idle value: PARA_SRC_ID; Timing / sampling: Constant; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_source must always equal PARA_SRC_ID.

rules.quote: Port: o_tlul_a_address; Direction: Output; Width: PARA_ADDR_W; Meaning (function): Request address: bits [PARA_ADDR_W-1:2] from flops, bits [1:0] constant 0; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Data (valid with o_tlul_a_valid); Reset / idle value: 0; Timing / sampling: Stable while valid; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_address bits [1:0] must be constant 0 and the address must be stable while o_tlul_a_valid is high.

rules.quote: Port: o_tlul_a_mask; Direction: Output (constant); Width: 4; Meaning (function): Byte lanes, always 4'b1111; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Static (constant 4'b1111); Reset / idle value: 4'b1111; Timing / sampling: Constant; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_mask must always be 4'b1111.

rules.quote: Port: o_tlul_a_data; Direction: Output (flop); Width: 32; Meaning (function): Write data (copy of PWDATA; unused by the device on Get); Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Data (valid with o_tlul_a_valid); Reset / idle value: 0; Timing / sampling: Stable while valid; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_data must be a copy of PWDATA and stable while o_tlul_a_valid is high.

rules.quote: Port: o_tlul_a_user; Direction: Output (constant); Width: PARA_A_USER_W; Meaning (function): A-channel user bits, always '0 (DEC-004); Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Static (constant 0); Reset / idle value: '0; Timing / sampling: Constant; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_user must always be '0.

rules.quote: Port: o_tlul_d_ready; Direction: Output (flop); Width: 1; Meaning (function): Response accepted; Clock domain: CLK-CORE; Signal type: Level (0 in reset, then constant 1); Reset / idle value: 0 in reset, then 1 (DEC-010); Timing / sampling: Constant 1 after the first clock edge following reset release; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_tlul_d_ready must be 0 in reset and constant 1 after the first clock edge following reset release.

rules.quote: Signal types: a level is held until it is acknowledged or changed; the only pulse is o_apb_pready, one cycle per transfer, which the APB requester samples in that cycle; data signals are qualified by the signal named in their type; static signals never change after reset.
rules.statement: Levels are held until acknowledged or changed; the only pulse is o_apb_pready, one cycle per transfer; static signals never change after reset.

rules.quote: The inputs i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink and i_tlul_d_user and the APB input i_apb_pprot are unused; they need a lint waiver (section 14.3).
rules.statement: Unused inputs need a lint waiver.

rules.quote: The Setup phase lasts one cycle (PSEL = 1, PENABLE = 0); the Access phase starts in the next cycle and lasts until PREADY is high (REF-001 4.1).
rules.statement: Setup phase lasts one cycle with PSEL=1 and PENABLE=0; the Access phase starts next cycle and lasts until PREADY is high.

rules.quote: The signals PADDR, PWRITE, PWDATA and PSTRB stay unchanged from Setup until PREADY (REF-001 3.1, 4.1), which lets the bridge capture them once, at the Setup edge.
rules.statement: PADDR, PWRITE, PWDATA and PSTRB stay unchanged from Setup until PREADY.

rules.quote: PSLVERR is only valid in the last cycle of the transfer (REF-001 3.4), and the bridge asserts it only together with PREADY.
rules.statement: The bridge asserts PSLVERR only together with PREADY.

rules.quote: PSTRB is LOW on reads (REF-001 3.2) and is ignored by the bridge on reads.
rules.statement: The bridge ignores PSTRB on reads.

rules.quote: Back-to-back transfers with i_apb_psel held high are supported (REQ-FUNC-008, section 5.3). Case: Next Setup phase right after PREADY, i_apb_psel held at 1; Legal behavior: Transfer accepted exactly like the first one; Illegal / unsupported case: None; IP response: Same results; Setup-to-Setup interval as in 10.4; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-008, REQ-PERF-004
rules.condition: next Setup phase right after PREADY with i_apb_psel held at 1
rules.statement: Back-to-back transfers with i_apb_psel held high are accepted exactly like the first transfer with the same results.

rules.quote: The bridge issues one request at a time.
rules.statement: The bridge issues one TL-UL request at a time.

rules.quote: The request is stable until accepted.
rules.condition: request issued and not yet accepted
rules.statement: The TL-UL request stays stable until accepted.

rules.quote: The bridge accepts a response at any time; a response that does not belong to an accepted request is discarded (REQ-FUNC-007), as the OpenTitan hosts do (REF-002, explicit error cases). Case: TL-UL response with no accepted request; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Orphan response; IP response: Discarded, no APB effect; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-007
rules.condition: TL-UL response with no accepted request
rules.statement: The bridge accepts responses at any time and discards a response not belonging to an accepted request, with no APB effect.

rules.quote: A response in the same cycle as the request acceptance is allowed by REF-005 and is supported.
rules.condition: response in same cycle as request acceptance
rules.statement: The bridge supports a TL-UL response in the same cycle as the request acceptance.

rules.quote: Case: Write, PSTRB = 4'b1111, aligned address; Legal behavior: PutFullData, size 2, mask 4'b1111; Illegal / unsupported case: None; IP response: Normal completion; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-002
rules.condition: Write with PSTRB=4'b1111 and aligned address
rules.statement: The bridge issues PutFullData, size 2, mask 4'b1111 and completes normally.

rules.quote: Case: Write, any other PSTRB (including 4'b0000); Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Not supported (DEC-001); IP response: PREADY = 1 with PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle; no TL-UL request; Requirement IDs: REQ-ERR-001
rules.statement: PREADY=1 with PSLVERR=1 in the first Access cycle and no TL-UL request is issued.

rules.quote: Case: Read, aligned address (any PSTRB value is ignored); Legal behavior: Get, size 2, mask 4'b1111; Illegal / unsupported case: None; IP response: Data on PRDATA; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-003
rules.statement: The bridge issues Get, size 2, mask 4'b1111 and returns data on PRDATA.

rules.quote: Case: Read or write, PADDR[1:0] not 2'b00; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Not supported; IP response: PREADY = 1 with PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle; no TL-UL request; Requirement IDs: REQ-ERR-002
rules.condition: Read or write with PADDR[1:0] not 2'b00
rules.statement: PREADY=1 with PSLVERR=1 in the first Access cycle and no TL-UL request is issued.

rules.quote: Case: TL-UL response with d_error = 1; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Error response; IP response: PSLVERR = 1, PRDATA = 0; Requirement IDs: REQ-ERR-003
rules.statement: PSLVERR=1 and PRDATA=0.

rules.quote: Case: TL-UL response with a wrong d_opcode or d_source; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Protocol error of the device; IP response: PSLVERR = 1, PRDATA = 0; Requirement IDs: REQ-ERR-004, REQ-ERR-005
rules.condition: TL-UL response with wrong d_opcode or d_source
rules.statement: PSLVERR=1 and PRDATA=0.

rules.quote: Crossing ID: Not applicable; From → to: Not applicable; Signals: Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-18): one clock domain and one reset domain, so no crossing; Structure: Not applicable; Reset handling: Not applicable; Constraints / verification: A CDC tool run reports zero crossings (TEST-016)
rules.statement: A CDC tool run must report zero crossings, since there is one clock domain and one reset domain.

rules.quote: Reset ID: RST-CORE; Port: i_rst_n_core; Polarity / assertion: Active-low; Sync or async: Asynchronous assertion; synchronous release provided by the SoC reset controller (REF-003 RST-02, DEP-002); Scope: All flip-flops; Deassertion: Synchronous to i_clk_core; Reset value: Both FSMs in ENUM_ST_IDLE; reg_a_valid, reg_d_ready, reg_pready, reg_pslverr, reg_prdata, reg_a_rd, reg_a_addr, reg_a_data = 0
rules.statement: i_rst_n_core is active-low, asserted asynchronously, and deasserted synchronously to i_clk_core (synchronous release provided by the SoC reset controller).

rules.quote: Reset ID: RST-CORE; Port: i_rst_n_core; Polarity / assertion: Active-low; Sync or async: Asynchronous assertion; synchronous release provided by the SoC reset controller (REF-003 RST-02, DEP-002); Scope: All flip-flops; Deassertion: Synchronous to i_clk_core; Reset value: Both FSMs in ENUM_ST_IDLE; reg_a_valid, reg_d_ready, reg_pready, reg_pslverr, reg_prdata, reg_a_rd, reg_a_addr, reg_a_data = 0 Every flip-flop has the asynchronous reset (DEC-013): both FSM state registers, reg_a_valid, reg_d_ready, reg_pready, reg_pslverr and reg_prdata, and also the payload registers reg_a_rd, reg_a_addr and reg_a_data.
rules.statement: Every flip-flop, including both FSM state registers and the payload registers, must be asynchronously reset; FSMs go to ENUM_ST_IDLE and all listed registers to 0.

rules.quote: All are reset to 0, so every flop-driven output is defined after reset: o_tlul_a_opcode = 3'b000, o_tlul_a_address = 0 and o_tlul_a_data = 0 while o_tlul_a_valid = 0. reg_d_ready is cleared by reset and its D input is 1, so o_tlul_d_ready becomes 1 at the first clock edge after reset release (DEC-010).
rules.statement: After reset, o_tlul_a_opcode must be 3'b000, o_tlul_a_address 0, o_tlul_a_data 0 and o_tlul_a_valid 0.

rules.quote: All are reset to 0, so every flop-driven output is defined after reset: o_tlul_a_opcode = 3'b000, o_tlul_a_address = 0 and o_tlul_a_data = 0 while o_tlul_a_valid = 0. reg_d_ready is cleared by reset and its D input is 1, so o_tlul_d_ready becomes 1 at the first clock edge after reset release (DEC-010).
rules.condition: At the first clock edge after reset release
rules.statement: o_tlul_d_ready must become 1 at the first clock edge after reset release.

rules.quote: A transfer in progress when the reset asserts is abandoned; the SoC resets the APB Requester and the TL-UL device together with the bridge (DEP-002).
rules.condition: A transfer is in progress when reset asserts
rules.statement: The transfer is abandoned, and the SoC resets the APB Requester and TL-UL device together with the bridge.

rules.quote: Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-18): the IP is in the always-on domain of the SoC and has no isolation, retention or power sequencing of its own.
rules.statement: The IP resides in the SoC always-on domain and has no isolation, retention or power sequencing of its own.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_ADDR_W; Purpose: Address width of both buses; Default: 32; Legal values / range: 16 to 32; Dependencies / invalid combinations: None; Effect: Width of i_apb_paddr and o_tlul_a_address
rules.statement: PARA_ADDR_W (default 32, legal range 16 to 32) shall set the width of both i_apb_paddr and o_tlul_a_address.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_SRC_W; Purpose: Width of the TL-UL source identifier; Default: 8; Legal values / range: 1 to 8; Dependencies / invalid combinations: PARA_SRC_ID shall fit in PARA_SRC_W bits; Effect: Width of o_tlul_a_source and i_tlul_d_source
rules.statement: PARA_SRC_W (default 8, legal range 1 to 8) shall set the width of o_tlul_a_source and i_tlul_d_source.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_SRC_W; Purpose: Width of the TL-UL source identifier; Default: 8; Legal values / range: 1 to 8; Dependencies / invalid combinations: PARA_SRC_ID shall fit in PARA_SRC_W bits; Effect: Width of o_tlul_a_source and i_tlul_d_source Parameter: PARA_SRC_ID; Purpose: Constant source identifier of every request; Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0 to 2^PARA_SRC_W - 1; Dependencies / invalid combinations: Shall fit in PARA_SRC_W bits; Effect: Value of o_tlul_a_source and of the expected i_tlul_d_source
rules.statement: PARA_SRC_ID shall fit in PARA_SRC_W bits, i.e. lie in the range 0 to 2^PARA_SRC_W - 1.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_SRC_ID; Purpose: Constant source identifier of every request; Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0 to 2^PARA_SRC_W - 1; Dependencies / invalid combinations: Shall fit in PARA_SRC_W bits; Effect: Value of o_tlul_a_source and of the expected i_tlul_d_source
rules.statement: The value of o_tlul_a_source on every request and the expected i_tlul_d_source shall equal PARA_SRC_ID (default 0).

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_A_USER_W; Purpose: Width of the a_user bits, which are always driven to zero (width only, ASM-005); Default: 1; Legal values / range: 1 to 32; Dependencies / invalid combinations: The layout of a_user depends on the integration project (TBD-001); the default is the lowest width because the bits are constant zero; Effect: Width of o_tlul_a_user
rules.statement: o_tlul_a_user shall have width PARA_A_USER_W (default 1, range 1 to 32) and its bits shall always be driven to zero.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_D_SINK_W; Purpose: Width of the unused d_sink input (width only); Default: 1; Legal values / range: 1 to 4; Dependencies / invalid combinations: None; Effect: Width of i_tlul_d_sink; no behavior
rules.statement: PARA_D_SINK_W (default 1, range 1 to 4) shall set the width of i_tlul_d_sink, which has no behavioral effect.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_D_USER_W; Purpose: Width of the unused d_user input (width only); Default: 1; Legal values / range: 1 to 32; Dependencies / invalid combinations: None; Effect: Width of i_tlul_d_user; no behavior
rules.statement: PARA_D_USER_W (default 1, range 1 to 32) shall set the width of i_tlul_d_user, which has no behavioral effect.

rules.quote: The module m_tlul_if also holds three constants that are not parameters and cannot be overridden: LPARA_A_SIZE = 2 (request size code, 4 bytes), LPARA_A_MASK = 4'b1111 (all byte lanes) and LPARA_D_ACK_DATA = 1 (d_opcode of AccessAckData).
rules.statement: m_tlul_if shall use fixed non-overridable constants LPARA_A_SIZE = 2, LPARA_A_MASK = 4'b1111 and LPARA_D_ACK_DATA = 1 (AccessAckData d_opcode).

rules.quote: An illegal parameter value shall be reported at elaboration of the verification source set and shall not be silently clamped.
rules.condition: An illegal parameter value is used
rules.statement: An illegal parameter value shall be reported at elaboration of the verification source set.

rules.quote: An illegal parameter value shall be reported at elaboration of the verification source set and shall not be silently clamped.
rules.condition: An illegal parameter value is used
rules.statement: An illegal parameter value shall not be silently clamped.

rules.quote: The data bus is 32 bits wide; byte lane i carries bits [8i+7:8i], and PSTRB[i] and a_mask[i] refer to the same lane.
rules.statement: Byte lane i of the 32-bit data bus carries bits [8i+7:8i], and PSTRB[i] and a_mask[i] refer to the same lane.

rules.quote: Quantity: APB address; Width: PARA_ADDR_W; Encoding / range: Byte address; bits [1:0] shall be 0; Extension / truncation: Bits [PARA_ADDR_W-1:2] are copied to a_address[PARA_ADDR_W-1:2]; a_address[1:0] = 2'b00; Overflow / invalid behavior: Non-zero bits [1:0] give PSLVERR (REQ-ERR-002)
rules.statement: APB address bits [1:0] shall be 0 (word-aligned byte address).

rules.quote: Quantity: APB address; Width: PARA_ADDR_W; Encoding / range: Byte address; bits [1:0] shall be 0; Extension / truncation: Bits [PARA_ADDR_W-1:2] are copied to a_address[PARA_ADDR_W-1:2]; a_address[1:0] = 2'b00; Overflow / invalid behavior: Non-zero bits [1:0] give PSLVERR (REQ-ERR-002)
rules.statement: Bits [PARA_ADDR_W-1:2] of the APB address are copied to a_address[PARA_ADDR_W-1:2], and a_address[1:0] is 2'b00.

rules.quote: Quantity: APB address; Width: PARA_ADDR_W; Encoding / range: Byte address; bits [1:0] shall be 0; Extension / truncation: Bits [PARA_ADDR_W-1:2] are copied to a_address[PARA_ADDR_W-1:2]; a_address[1:0] = 2'b00; Overflow / invalid behavior: Non-zero bits [1:0] give PSLVERR (REQ-ERR-002)
rules.statement: A non-zero value in APB address bits [1:0] shall give PSLVERR (REQ-ERR-002).

rules.quote: Quantity: a_opcode; Width: 3; Encoding / range: 3'b000 PutFullData, 3'b100 Get; Extension / truncation: Bit 2 = read, bits [1:0] = 0; Overflow / invalid behavior: Other values are never generated
rules.statement: a_opcode shall be 3'b000 (PutFullData) for writes and 3'b100 (Get) for reads, with bit 2 as read and bits [1:0] zero.

rules.quote: Quantity: a_opcode; Width: 3; Encoding / range: 3'b000 PutFullData, 3'b100 Get; Extension / truncation: Bit 2 = read, bits [1:0] = 0; Overflow / invalid behavior: Other values are never generated
rules.statement: a_opcode values other than 3'b000 and 3'b100 shall never be generated.

rules.quote: Quantity: a_size; Width: 2; Encoding / range: 2'b10 (4 bytes); Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Other values are never generated
rules.statement: a_size shall be 2'b10 (4 bytes) and no other value shall ever be generated.

rules.quote: Quantity: a_mask; Width: 4; Encoding / range: 4'b1111; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Other values are never generated (DEC-001)
rules.statement: a_mask shall be 4'b1111 and no other value shall ever be generated (DEC-001).

rules.quote: Quantity: d_opcode; Width: 3; Encoding / range: 3'b000 AccessAck, 3'b001 AccessAckData; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Any value other than the expected one gives PSLVERR
rules.condition: d_opcode differs from the expected value (3'b000 AccessAck for writes, 3'b001 AccessAckData for reads)
rules.statement: Any d_opcode value other than the expected one shall give PSLVERR.

rules.quote: Quantity: Read data; Width: 32; Encoding / range: Unsigned word; Extension / truncation: Forced to 0 for writes and for every error completion; Overflow / invalid behavior: Not applicable
rules.condition: write transfer or any error completion
rules.statement: Read data shall be forced to 0 for writes and for every error completion.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_IDLE; Entry condition: Reset release, or end of ENUM_ST_DONE; Behavior: Waits for the Setup phase (i_apb_psel = 1, i_apb_penable = 0); Exit condition: Legal request: ENUM_ST_BUSY. Illegal request: ENUM_ST_DONE; Outputs / side effects: Legal: w_req_launch = 1. Illegal: reg_pready, reg_pslverr set, reg_prdata cleared at the Setup edge
rules.condition: APB FSM in ENUM_ST_IDLE, Setup phase (i_apb_psel = 1, i_apb_penable = 0) with a legal request
rules.statement: The APB FSM must go to ENUM_ST_BUSY and assert w_req_launch = 1 on a legal request in the Setup phase.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_IDLE; Entry condition: Reset release, or end of ENUM_ST_DONE; Behavior: Waits for the Setup phase (i_apb_psel = 1, i_apb_penable = 0); Exit condition: Legal request: ENUM_ST_BUSY. Illegal request: ENUM_ST_DONE; Outputs / side effects: Legal: w_req_launch = 1. Illegal: reg_pready, reg_pslverr set, reg_prdata cleared at the Setup edge
rules.condition: APB FSM in ENUM_ST_IDLE, Setup phase with an illegal request
rules.statement: The APB FSM must go to ENUM_ST_DONE, set reg_pready and reg_pslverr and clear reg_prdata at the Setup edge on an illegal request.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_BUSY; Entry condition: Legal request launched; Behavior: Waits for w_resp_valid; Exit condition: w_resp_valid = 1: ENUM_ST_DONE; Outputs / side effects: At that edge reg_pready, reg_pslverr and reg_prdata load the response
rules.condition: APB FSM in ENUM_ST_BUSY and w_resp_valid = 1
rules.statement: The APB FSM must move to ENUM_ST_DONE, and reg_pready, reg_pslverr and reg_prdata must load the response at that edge.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_REQ; Entry condition: Request launched; Behavior: o_tlul_a_valid = 1; channel A stable; Exit condition: i_tlul_a_ready = 1 with a valid response in the same cycle: ENUM_ST_IDLE; i_tlul_a_ready = 1 without response: ENUM_ST_WAIT; Outputs / side effects: reg_a_valid cleared when the request is accepted
rules.statement: The TL-UL FSM must hold o_tlul_a_valid = 1 with channel A stable in ENUM_ST_REQ, clear reg_a_valid on acceptance, and go to IDLE with a same-cycle response or WAIT without.

rules.quote: A response counts only in ENUM_ST_WAIT, or in ENUM_ST_REQ together with i_tlul_a_ready = 1.
rules.statement: A response must count only in ENUM_ST_WAIT, or in ENUM_ST_REQ together with i_tlul_a_ready = 1.

rules.quote: A d_valid in any other state is an orphan and is discarded (REQ-FUNC-007).
rules.condition: d_valid arrives in any state other than WAIT or REQ with a_ready
rules.statement: An orphan i_tlul_d_valid in any other state must be discarded with no APB effect.

rules.quote: Waveform ID: WF-003; Function / operation: OP-003 illegal request, local error; Scenario (success / error / corner): error; Signals shown: PSTRB, PREADY and PSLVERR in the first Access cycle, no channel A request; Figure: figures/apb_local_err.svg (Figure 12-2); Confirmed by user: 2026-10-21
rules.statement: For an illegal request, PREADY and PSLVERR must be asserted in the first Access cycle with no channel A request.

rules.quote: Waveform ID: WF-005; Function / operation: OP-001 and OP-002 with channel A back pressure; Scenario (success / error / corner): corner; Signals shown: a_ready low, channel A stable, extended Access phase; Figure: figures/tlul_backpressure.svg (Figure 6-3); Confirmed by user: 2026-10-21
rules.statement: With channel A back pressure, channel A must remain stable and the Access phase is extended.

rules.quote: Cycle / event: S (Setup); Input condition: i_apb_psel = 1, i_apb_penable = 0, legal request; State/action: At the end of S: channel A flops load, reg_a_valid set, APB FSM to ENUM_ST_BUSY, TL-UL FSM to ENUM_ST_REQ; Output condition: All outputs idle (o_apb_pready = 0, o_tlul_a_valid = 0)
rules.statement: At the end of S, channel A flops must load, reg_a_valid set, APB FSM go to BUSY and TL-UL FSM to REQ, with o_apb_pready and o_tlul_a_valid 0 in S.

rules.quote: Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-18): the bridge has no software-visible registers.
rules.statement: The bridge has no software-visible registers; none are required or provided.

rules.quote: It is configured only by parameters (section 8), and its only status is PSLVERR on each transfer.
rules.statement: The bridge's only status indication is PSLVERR on each transfer; it is otherwise configured only by parameters.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-001; Detection condition: Write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111; Observable response/status: PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle; PRDATA = 0; no TL-UL request; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The next transfer is independent; Reset behavior: Not applicable (no stored error)
rules.condition: APB write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111 (ERR-001)
rules.statement: The bridge must respond in the first Access cycle with PREADY = 1, PSLVERR = 1 and PRDATA = 0.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-001; Detection condition: Write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111; Observable response/status: PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle; PRDATA = 0; no TL-UL request; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The next transfer is independent; Reset behavior: Not applicable (no stored error)
rules.condition: APB write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111 (ERR-001)
rules.statement: The bridge must not issue a TL-UL request for a write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-001; Detection condition: Write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111; Observable response/status: PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle; PRDATA = 0; no TL-UL request; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The next transfer is independent; Reset behavior: Not applicable (no stored error)
rules.statement: The next transfer must be independent of the error; no error state is stored and reset behavior is not applicable.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-002; Detection condition: PADDR[1:0] not 2'b00; Observable response/status: Same as ERR-001; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Same; Reset behavior: Same
rules.statement: The bridge must respond as for ERR-001: PREADY = 1, PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle, PRDATA = 0, and no TL-UL request.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-003; Detection condition: i_tlul_d_error = 1 on the accepted response; Observable response/status: PSLVERR = 1, PRDATA = 0, with PREADY; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Same; Reset behavior: Same
rules.statement: The bridge must drive PSLVERR = 1 and PRDATA = 0 together with PREADY.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-003; Detection condition: i_tlul_d_error = 1 on the accepted response; Observable response/status: PSLVERR = 1, PRDATA = 0, with PREADY; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Same; Reset behavior: Same Error ID: ERR-004; Detection condition: d_opcode not equal to the expected opcode; Observable response/status: Same as ERR-003; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Same; Reset behavior: Same Error ID: ERR-005; Detection condition: d_source not equal to PARA_SRC_ID; Observable response/status: Same as ERR-003; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Same; Reset behavior: Same
rules.condition: After an ERR-003, ERR-004 or ERR-005 error transfer
rules.statement: The next transfer must be independent of the error, with no stored error state.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-004; Detection condition: d_opcode not equal to the expected opcode; Observable response/status: Same as ERR-003; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Same; Reset behavior: Same
rules.condition: d_opcode is not equal to the expected opcode (ERR-004)
rules.statement: The bridge must drive PSLVERR = 1 and PRDATA = 0 together with PREADY, as for ERR-003.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-005; Detection condition: d_source not equal to PARA_SRC_ID; Observable response/status: Same as ERR-003; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Same; Reset behavior: Same
rules.condition: d_source is not equal to PARA_SRC_ID (ERR-005)
rules.statement: The bridge must drive PSLVERR = 1 and PRDATA = 0 together with PREADY, as for ERR-003.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-006; Detection condition: No response ever arrives; Observable response/status: The APB Requester waits (no PREADY); Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Handled by the SoC watchdog (DEC-003); reset of the bridge, the Requester and the device recovers; Reset behavior: Reset abandons the transfer
rules.statement: The bridge must not assert PREADY; the APB Requester waits, and recovery is by SoC watchdog or reset.

rules.quote: All detected errors give the same result, PSLVERR = 1 with PRDATA = 0, so no priority between them is needed.
rules.statement: All detected errors must give the same result, PSLVERR = 1 with PRDATA = 0, with no priority between them.

rules.quote: The bridge keeps no sticky error flag in the RTL: errors are visible only on PSLVERR.
rules.statement: The bridge RTL must keep no sticky error flag; errors are visible only on PSLVERR.

rules.quote: Metric ID: PERF-001; Metric: Access-phase length, normal transfer; Target / limit: 3 cycles (2 wait states); Conditions: Device accepts in A1 and responds in A2; Measurement method: Simulation TEST-002, TEST-006; Hard / goal: Hard (REQ-PERF-001)
rules.condition: Device accepts in A1 and responds in A2 on a normal transfer
rules.statement: The access phase of a normal transfer must last 3 cycles (2 wait states).

rules.quote: Metric ID: PERF-002; Metric: Access-phase length, same-cycle response; Target / limit: 2 cycles (1 wait state); Conditions: Device responds in the acceptance cycle; Measurement method: Simulation TEST-011; Hard / goal: Hard (REQ-PERF-002)
rules.condition: Device responds in the acceptance cycle
rules.statement: The access phase for a same-cycle response must last 2 cycles (1 wait state).

rules.quote: Metric ID: PERF-003; Metric: Access-phase length, local error; Target / limit: 1 cycle (0 wait states); Conditions: Illegal strobe or address; Measurement method: Simulation TEST-004, TEST-005; Hard / goal: Hard (REQ-PERF-003)
rules.condition: Illegal strobe or address causes a local error
rules.statement: The access phase of a local error must last 1 cycle (0 wait states).

rules.quote: Metric ID: PERF-004; Metric: Minimum transfer interval; Target / limit: 4 cycles normal, 3 same-cycle response, 2 local error; the same when i_apb_psel is held high; Conditions: As above; Measurement method: Simulation TEST-013, TEST-019; Hard / goal: Hard
rules.condition: Also when i_apb_psel is held high
rules.statement: The minimum transfer interval must be 4 cycles for normal, 3 for same-cycle response, and 2 for local error transfers.

rules.quote: The VLSIT RTL Design Rules v2 in VLSIT_RTL_Design_Rule.md (REF-003) are the mandatory RTL coding authority.
rules.statement: The RTL must follow the VLSIT RTL Design Rules v2 (REF-003) as the mandatory RTL coding authority.

rules.quote: The RTL complies with it without local exceptions.
rules.statement: The RTL must comply with the VLSIT RTL Design Rules without local exceptions.

rules.statement: Coding style: one module per file named as the module, structural top, ANSI ports with input wire and output logic, reg_/w_/p_ff_/p_com_ names, PARA_* parameters with three PAR-02 comment lines, names at most 30 characters, comment lines at most 100 characters.

rules.quote: Module: m_apb_tlul_bridge; Responsibility: Structural top: ports, parameters, interconnect wires and the two instances only; Parent / instance: Top; Clock/reset domains: CLK-CORE / RST-CORE; Interface: All ports of section 6.2
rules.statement: m_apb_tlul_bridge is the structural top containing only ports, parameters, interconnect wires and the two instances, in CLK-CORE/RST-CORE domains.

rules.quote: Module: m_apb_if; Responsibility: All APB-facing logic: Setup detect, legality check, APB FSM, response flops (reg_pready, reg_pslverr, reg_prdata); Parent / instance: m_apb_tlul_bridge / u_apb_if; Clock/reset domains: CLK-CORE / RST-CORE; Interface: APB4 Completer ports and the internal wires of section 5.1
rules.statement: m_apb_if, instance u_apb_if, must contain all APB-facing logic: Setup detect, legality check, APB FSM and response flops reg_pready, reg_pslverr, reg_prdata.

rules.quote: Module: m_tlul_if; Responsibility: All TL-UL-facing logic: channel A flops, TL-UL FSM, reg_d_ready, D-channel check; Parent / instance: m_apb_tlul_bridge / u_tlul_if; Clock/reset domains: CLK-CORE / RST-CORE; Interface: TL-UL host ports and the internal wires of section 5.1
rules.statement: m_tlul_if, instance u_tlul_if, must contain all TL-UL-facing logic: channel A flops, TL-UL FSM, reg_d_ready and D-channel check.

rules.quote: State is owned by m_apb_if and m_tlul_if. m_apb_if has no TL-UL port and m_tlul_if has no APB port (REQ-IF-007).
rules.statement: State is owned by m_apb_if and m_tlul_if; m_apb_if has no TL-UL port and m_tlul_if has no APB port.

rules.quote: Item: Lint rule configuration; Value / source: The project lint set with default_nettype none checking; waiver for the unused inputs i_apb_pprot, i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink, i_tlul_d_user
rules.statement: Lint uses the project lint set with default_nettype none checking, waiving only the unused inputs i_apb_pprot, i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink, i_tlul_d_user.

rules.quote: The environment has an APB Requester model that drives legal and illegal requests and varies the idle time between transfers, and a TL-UL device model that delays a_ready and d_valid, answers in the acceptance cycle, injects d_error, wrong opcode and wrong source, and sends orphan responses.
rules.statement: The environment includes an APB Requester model driving legal/illegal requests with varied idle time, and a TL-UL device model delaying a_ready and d_valid, answering in acceptance cycle, injecting d_error, wrong opcode, wrong source and orphan responses.

rules.quote: The APB protocol checker and the TL-UL protocol checker of REF-005 are bound at the ports.
rules.statement: The APB protocol checker and the TL-UL protocol checker of REF-005 are bound at the ports.

rules.quote: A scoreboard compares each TL-UL request and each APB completion with the APB transfer that caused it.
rules.statement: A scoreboard compares each TL-UL request and each APB completion with the APB transfer that caused it.

rules.quote: Each run records its seed.
rules.statement: Each simulation run records its seed.

rules.quote: The acceptance criterion is that every requirement in section 3 is covered by at least one passing test and that all coverage bins of 15.3 are hit.
rules.statement: Every requirement in section 3 is covered by at least one passing test and all coverage bins of 15.3 are hit.

rules.quote: Test ID: TEST-001; Requirements: REQ-RESET-001, REQ-IF-006; Scenario / stimulus: Assert and release reset; observe outputs; Expected result: All listed outputs 0 in reset (including o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address, o_tlul_a_data); o_tlul_d_ready becomes 1 at the first edge after release; Test type: Directed; Configuration: CFG-BASE
rules.condition: during reset and after reset release
rules.statement: All listed outputs are 0 in reset, including o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address and o_tlul_a_data; o_tlul_d_ready becomes 1 at the first edge after release.

rules.quote: Test ID: TEST-002; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-001, REQ-FUNC-002, REQ-FUNC-006, REQ-PERF-001; Scenario / stimulus: Aligned write with PSTRB = 4'b1111 to a prompt device; Expected result: PutFullData, size 2, mask 4'b1111, address and data correct; 3 Access cycles; PRDATA = 0; Test type: Directed; Configuration: CFG-BASE
rules.condition: aligned write with PSTRB=4'b1111 to a prompt device
rules.statement: Bridge issues PutFullData, size 2, mask 4'b1111 with correct address and data, completes in 3 Access cycles, and PRDATA is 0.

rules.quote: Test ID: TEST-003; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-002, REQ-FUNC-003; Scenario / stimulus: Random aligned reads and writes with random data; Expected result: Scoreboard matches every request and completion; Test type: Constrained random; Configuration: CFG-BASE, CFG-NARROW
rules.statement: Scoreboard matches every TL-UL request and APB completion for random aligned reads and writes.

rules.quote: Test ID: TEST-004; Requirements: REQ-ERR-001, REQ-PERF-003; Scenario / stimulus: Write with each of the 15 PSTRB values other than 4'b1111; Expected result: No TL-UL request; PREADY and PSLVERR in the first Access cycle; PRDATA = 0; Test type: Directed; Configuration: CFG-BASE Test ID: TEST-005; Requirements: REQ-ERR-002, REQ-PERF-003; Scenario / stimulus: Reads and writes with PADDR[1:0] = 2'b01, 2'b10, 2'b11; Expected result: Same as TEST-004; Test type: Directed; Configuration: CFG-BASE
rules.condition: write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111, or access with PADDR[1:0] nonzero
rules.statement: No TL-UL request is issued; PREADY and PSLVERR are asserted in the first Access cycle and PRDATA is 0.

rules.quote: Test ID: TEST-006; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-001, REQ-FUNC-003, REQ-FUNC-006, REQ-PERF-001; Scenario / stimulus: Read with random data, PSTRB = 4'b0000 and also non-zero (ignored); Expected result: Get; PRDATA equals d_data; 3 Access cycles; Test type: Directed and random; Configuration: CFG-BASE
rules.statement: Bridge issues Get, ignores PSTRB, PRDATA equals d_data, and completes in 3 Access cycles.

rules.quote: Test ID: TEST-007; Requirements: REQ-ERR-003, REQ-FUNC-006; Scenario / stimulus: Response with d_error = 1 on a read and on a write; Expected result: PSLVERR = 1; PRDATA = 0; Test type: Directed; Configuration: CFG-BASE
rules.condition: response with d_error = 1 on read or write
rules.statement: PSLVERR is 1 and PRDATA is 0.

rules.quote: Test ID: TEST-008; Requirements: REQ-ERR-004, REQ-ERR-005; Scenario / stimulus: Wrong d_opcode, and wrong d_source (CFG-NARROW uses PARA_SRC_ID = 1); Expected result: PSLVERR = 1; PRDATA = 0; Test type: Directed; Configuration: CFG-BASE, CFG-NARROW
rules.statement: PSLVERR is 1 and PRDATA is 0.

rules.quote: Test ID: TEST-009; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-005; Scenario / stimulus: Random delays on a_ready (0 to 8 cycles); Expected result: Channel A stable while valid and not ready; request accepted once; Test type: Constrained random; Configuration: CFG-BASE
